t: You're looking at Pelham Crescent, numbers one to fourteen, a curved terrace of houses in Kensington and Chelsea. It was designed by George Basevi, an English architect who trained under Sir John Soane. Basevi worked in both Neoclassical and Gothic Revival styles. He is best known for Belgrave Square in London and the Fitzwilliam Museum in Cambridge. He also served as surveyor to the Thurloe estate, which is the land around here. Look at the sweep of the crescent and how the houses sit together as one composition.
